realtime.title: Realtime
realtime.field_hint: Matches literal keys first, then nested paths such as app.name.
realtime.fallback_hint: Where an event goes when the field is missing, is not text, or does not make a stream name.
realtime.auto_create: A stream that does not exist yet is created by the first event written to it.
realtime.retain_hint: Keep the original log in {{source}} after routing (masking still applies). Write once when source and destination match.
realtime.no_backfill: Realtime pipelines run on intake and do not support backfill.
realtime.in_place_rum: RUM events are changed as they arrive and stay in this stream. Only context, usr.extra, feature_flags and extra can change: every other column is what the RUM pages read, and a step that changes one fails the event. Actions, errors, resources and long tasks may be dropped; views and vitals never are.
realtime.in_place_metrics: Samples are changed as they arrive and stay in this stream. Labels can be removed, renamed or added to cut cardinality; a changed label makes a new series. The metric name, the value, count, sum, min and max, the time, the metric's metadata and the le and quantile labels are kept as they arrive: a step that changes one fails the sample.
realtime.in_place_profiles: Only a profile's metadata row goes through the steps; the profile itself stays as it was stored. Steps can rename the service, change labels, add fields and drop rows; a dropped row takes the profile out of the Profiles pages, and its object is removed when the retention period ends. The object's location, the ID, the type, the time and the measured values are kept as they arrive: a step that changes one fails the row.
realtime.in_place_traces: Spans are changed as they arrive, after tail sampling, and stay in this stream. Steps can drop spans, sample whole traces by trace_id, and remove or change attributes; an attribute changed here is changed in the span's attributes too. Trace and span IDs, the parent, service.name and the timing are kept as they arrive: a step that changes one fails the span. A span dropped from the middle of a trace leaves its children without a parent, and the trace list and the service map count only the spans that are written.

processing.output_hint: The routing step chooses the stream for each event. A stream that does not exist yet is created by the first event written to it.

settings.reliability_hint: A failed read or write is retried on the same stretch of time after 30 s, then twice as long each time up to the run interval, and skipped when the retries run out; a failed delivery is retried within the run. Events a step fails on, a stream rejects or a connector does not take go to the dead letter stream (logs) with the stage and the reason. Dedupe works within one run.
settings.realtime_note: Runs on every log event as it is ingested: one source stream, one destination, no schedule.
settings.realtime_note_metrics: Runs on every sample as it is written, in the stream it arrives in: one source stream, no schedule.
settings.realtime_note_traces: Runs on every span as it is written, after tail sampling, in the stream it arrives in: one source stream, no schedule.
settings.realtime_note_profiles: Runs on the metadata row of every profile as it is stored, in the stream it arrives in. The profile itself is not touched.

auth.label: Authentication

hints.access_key: A long-lived key of an IAM user. Give that user only what this connector needs.
hints.temporary_key: A short-lived key from AWS STS, valid only together with its session token. It stops working when it expires and has to be replaced here.
hints.node_role: No key is stored. MoleSignal uses the identity of the node it runs on: EKS IRSA or Pod Identity, an ECS task role, or an EC2 instance profile. Every organization in this deployment can choose it.
hints.sasl_plain: SASL/PLAIN sends the user name and password as they are: without TLS, use it on a private network only.
hints.none: For a broker that asks for no credentials.
hints.push_token: The other service presents this token with every push. Whoever holds it can write to the stream.
hints.node_role_s3: No key is stored. MoleSignal uses the identity of the node it runs on: EKS IRSA or Pod Identity, an ECS task role, or an EC2 instance profile. It needs s3:PutObject on the bucket, and every organization in this deployment can choose it.
hints.node_role_aws_cloudwatch_logs: No key is stored. MoleSignal uses the identity of the node it runs on: EKS IRSA or Pod Identity, an ECS task role, or an EC2 instance profile. It needs logs:FilterLogEvents on the log group, and every organization in this deployment can choose it.
hints.assume_role: MoleSignal assumes this role through AWS STS and renews its temporary key every hour. It assumes the role as the node's identity, or with an access key if you give one. The role's trust policy has to allow that identity and require the external ID below.
hints.web_identity: MoleSignal assumes this role with the web identity token on the node, such as the service account token EKS projects for IRSA (its path is in AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE). The role's trust policy has to trust the OIDC provider that issues the token.
hints.sasl_scram_sha_256: SASL/SCRAM-SHA-256: the password itself never crosses the network.
hints.sasl_scram_sha_512: SASL/SCRAM-SHA-512: the password itself never crosses the network. Amazon MSK uses this one.
hints.mtls: The client proves who it is with a certificate (mutual TLS), which needs TLS on. The certificate and its key are PEM; the key cannot be encrypted.
hints.bearer: Every request carries an Authorization: Bearer <token> header.
hints.basic: Every request carries an HTTP Basic authorization header; use it over https.
hints.header: The key travels in a header the receiver names, such as X-API-Key or DD-API-KEY.
hints.hmac: Every request carries X-MoleSignal-Timestamp (Unix seconds) and X-MoleSignal-Sign: sha256=<hex>, the HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<body>" under the shared secret. The receiver computes it again with the same secret and refuses an old timestamp.

auth.external_id_hint: This organization assumes roles with this external ID, which cannot be changed. Require it in the role's trust policy with an sts:ExternalId condition, and no other organization can assume the role even if it learns the ARN.
auth.base_key: Assume it with an access key, not the node's identity
auth.base_key_hint: For a deployment that does not run on AWS: an IAM user's key assumes the role.

hints.region_s3: The bucket's region. An S3-compatible store may not need one.
hints.region_s3_source: The bucket's region. An S3-compatible store may not need one.
hints.prefix_s3_source: Only objects under this prefix are read. Each read lists it, so give a source a prefix of its own.
hints.startFrom: Applies to the first read only; after that it goes on from where it left off.
hints.topic_kafka_source: Read with assigned partitions, not as a consumer group: the topic's read permission is enough.
hints.brokers: Host and port. Separate several with commas.
hints.endpoint: The store's S3 API address, starting with http:// or https://.
hints.url: Where the events are sent, starting with http:// or https://. An address often carries a credential, so it is kept like one: once saved, only its host is shown.

alert_mode.title: Alert events
alert_mode.list_line: Alert events → back into the incident
alert_mode.note: Runs on every alert event its conditions take, before the incident opens. Alert pipelines run in order, lowest first.
alert_mode.note_notify: Runs on a copy of the event when a notification policy is about to send. Alert pipelines run in order, lowest first.
alert_mode.write_back_notify_detail: The policy sends what the steps leave
alert_mode.write_back_notify_hint: The policy sends the title, severity, labels, annotations and services the steps leave, in its templates and webhooks too. The incident stays as it is, and so do the people the policy reaches. A step that drops the event with abort keeps this policy from sending: the delivery record says why. When a step fails, the changes of this pipeline are left out and the notification goes on as it came.

stage.label: When
stage.open_hint: What the steps leave is the incident: its team, its policy and every notification follow from it.
stage.notify_hint: Runs on a copy of the event, for each policy it applies to. Only that policy's notification changes, and steps stay inside MoleSignal: no AI summary, API call or query.

alert_mode.policies_hint: Tick none to run before every policy of an alert event.
alert_mode.policies_none: There is no notification policy of an alert event yet.

http.connector_hint: Its address, credential and outbound checks are used. Create one under Connectors.
http.none: There is no HTTP connector yet.
http.note: The event and where it came from are posted as JSON when the incident opens; the answer has 5 seconds. Of the JSON object that comes back, only summary, severity, priority, urgency, labels, annotations and affected_services are taken, labels and annotations key by key. If the call fails, the event goes on as it was before this step, and the incident's timeline says why.

query.stream_hint: The stream the query reads. _audit cannot be read here.
query.statement_hint: {{placeholders}} stand for values of the event. Write them between quotes, inside a string: that is where their values are escaped.
query.window_hint: Up to the moment the incident opens.
query.max_rows_hint: How many rows go into the annotation, up to {{max}}.
query.annotation_hint: The annotation the rows go into, one line per row. No rows leave it out.

alert_mode.write_back_detail: The incident opens as the steps leave it
alert_mode.no_backfill: Alert pipelines run on alert events as they come and do not support backfill.
alert_mode.no_steps: No steps: the incident opens as the alert event came.
alert_mode.test_no_steps: This pipeline has no steps: the incident opens as the alert event came.
alert_mode.write_back_hint: The incident opens with the title, severity, labels, annotations and services the steps leave. A step that drops the event with abort keeps the incident from opening. When a step fails, the changes of this pipeline are left out and the event goes on as it came.
alert_mode.source_hint: Which alert events this pipeline takes. Leave a list empty to take every one. A label condition matches when the event has the label with this value.
alert_mode.prompt_hint: Sent to the organization's model with the alert event. The model is asked once, when the incident opens, within the organization's daily token budget.
alert_mode.annotation_hint: The annotation the answer goes into.
alert_mode.time_hint: Judged at the moment the incident opens; for example, drop one kind of alert only at night.

table_sink.hint: Every event becomes a row under the value of its {{key}} field. A table with value fields takes those fields only.
table_sink.choose: Choose the extend table to write a row per event into.
table_sink.none: There is no extend table yet. Make one under Extend tables first.

counting.conditions_none: Every event. Add a test to pick only some.
counting.metric_name_hint: What PromQL selects it by. A histogram adds _bucket, _count and _sum.
counting.metric_sum_field_hint: Empty counts events; a numeric field adds up its values.
counting.metric_field_hint: An event without a number in it is not counted.
counting.group_by_hint: Each field becomes a label: one series per combination, at most 1,000 an interval.
counting.metric_stream_hint: Where the samples are written. A new name creates the stream.
counting.interval_hint: An event counts in the interval of its own timestamp.
counting.buckets_hint: Ascending, in the field's unit. +Inf is always there.
counting.query_hint: How PromQL, a dashboard or an alert rule reads it.
counting.over_target_hint: Events go there as this step sees them; the steps after it do not run on them.
counting.quota_limit_hint: Per UTC day; the count starts over at 00:00 UTC.
counting.partition_by_hint: Each combination of values is a bucket with its own count, at most 1,000 a day.
counting.overrides: Buckets with a limit of their own
counting.throttle_limit_hint: After a quiet window this many go through at once, then one every window ÷ limit.
counting.throttle_group_by_hint: Each combination of values is throttled on its own, at most 10,000 groups.

test.not_picked: Not picked by its condition: goes on untouched.
test.limit: Counts in {{bucket}} ({{limit}}); past the limit it is {{past}}.

usage.title: Limits today
usage.description: What each quota and throttle let through and held back today (UTC), across all nodes. Updated every few seconds.
